title: Scripture of a rite, pattern Mark I
description: A named liturgy that brings the machine into one of its aspects, kept in the rites/ hall of the Librarium; the rite bears the name of its scripture. Only the form of each key is judged here; recite 'servitor inquisition' for the full judgement of the Inquisition, and 'servitor expound <key>' for the lore of any key.

pattern.description: The Mark of the form in which this scripture is written. This servitor reads only "Mark I"; scripture of no pattern, or of another, is heresy.

purpose.description: The words that tell a reader why the rite exists, shown by the census and the cogitator. Never illuminated.

aspects.description: The named conditions the rite can bring the machine into, written by hand: at least one, each named once.

inscriptions.description: Named words carried by one invocation, spoken as the rune --<key>, illuminated as {{inscription.<key>}} and kept on the data-slate. Each key names one inscription.

not.description: The runes the servitor bears for its own rituals, which no inscription may take as its name.

auspex.description: The rite's own scanning words, telling which aspect the machine bears: a command whose words name the aspect, or {"rite": "<command>", "patience": "5s"}. It sees the aspect being invoked as {{aspect}} and SERVITOR_ASPECT.

tongue.description: The program in which this rite's incantations and litanies are spoken, unless a step names its own; the settings' tongue, else bash, when unwritten.

liturgy.description: The ordered steps the rite performs, one after another as written. Should one fall, every step already performed is reverted.

$schema.description: The schema this scripture is written against, for the editors of the faithful. The servitor accepts it and heeds it not.

name.description: A name fit for an aspect or an inscription: a letter or digit, then only letters, digits, '.', '_' or '-'.

aspectKey.description: A key of an aspect map: a declared aspect, or "*" to serve every aspect not named.

word.description: Words that may not be empty, for the servitor cannot perform what names nothing.

command.description: Words that may not be empty, in which placeholders such as {{aspect}} are filled at invocation.

patience.description: How long a command may labour before it is deemed to have fallen: a span greater than nothing, such as "500ms", "5s" or "2m".

inscription.description: One inscription of the rite: why it exists, whether an invocation may proceed without it, and the word each aspect decrees when the invocation gives none.

purpose.description: The words that tell a reader why the inscription exists, shown beside its rune.

mandatory.description: Whether an invocation must carry this inscription, by its rune or by a decree; an invocation without it then falls in the pre-flight.

decrees.description: The word each aspect inscribes when the invocation gives none: one word for every aspect, or an aspect map that may leave aspects without decree.

auspex.description: The long form of the auspex: its command, and how long it may labour.

rite.description: The command that names the aspect the machine bears; an answer that is no declared aspect yields no omen.

patience.description: How long the auspex may labour before it yields no omen.

tome.description: Scripture drawn from another scripture-file rather than written inline, read anew in every pre-flight.
The path of the tome; a path that does not begin at the root is reckoned from the hall of the rite's scripture.

illuminate.description: Whether the placeholders within the tome are filled; else its scripture is placed verbatim.

scripture.description: What a sanctum or transcription places into its vessel: inline words, a list of lines joined as one, or a tome.

sanctumScripture.description: The scripture a sanctum keeps: one for every aspect, or an aspect map. A sanctum's scripture may never be null; write "" to keep it empty.

transcriptionScripture.description: The scripture of a transcribed vessel: one for every aspect, or an aspect map; null strikes the vessel from the machine.

commands.description: Words that may differ per aspect: one for every aspect, or an aspect map.

verses.description: Words that may differ per aspect and may be empty: one for every aspect, or an aspect map.

anchor.description: Where a tether leads for each aspect: a path, or null to unbind it; one for every aspect, or an aspect map.

zeal.description: Leave for a step to overwrite what the servitor did not itself create.

step.description: One step of the liturgy, named by exactly one key of its kind.

sanctum.description: A step that keeps a warded region of a vessel and rewrites it alone, appending it to the vessel when not yet kept. Its marker records the aspect.
The vessel the sanctum is kept in: a scripture-file of the machine. A leading "~" and $NAMES are expanded.

ward.description: The name that marks this sanctum within its vessel; the rite's name when unwritten. No whitespace.

glyph.description: The mark that opens the sanctum's markers in the vessel's own tongue, such as "//" or "#"; divined from the vessel's name when unwritten.

closing-glyph.description: The mark that seals the sanctum's markers where remarks must be closed, such as "*/"; divined with the glyph when unwritten.

consecrate.description: Leave to bring the vessel into being should it be missing; its halls must already stand.

scripture.description: The scripture the sanctum keeps for each aspect.

transcription.description: A step that writes a whole vessel anew for each aspect, or strikes it. It replaces only a vessel holding the scripture of one of the rite's aspects, unless it burns with zeal.
The vessel written anew. A leading "~" and $NAMES are expanded.

scripture.description: The scripture of the vessel for each aspect, or null where the vessel shall not be.

seal.description: The rights of reading, writing and execution the vessel is to bear, as three or four octal numerals such as "0644"; a vessel already standing keeps its own.

zeal.description: Leave to overwrite what the servitor did not itself create; without it the pre-flight refuses.

force.description: The same leave as "zeal" under another name; write "zeal", never both.

tether.description: A step that binds a name in the machine to an anchor elsewhere. It rebinds only a tether, unless it burns with zeal.
The name bound. A leading "~" and $NAMES are expanded.

anchor.description: Where the tether leads for each aspect, or null to unbind it.

zeal.description: Leave to overwrite what the servitor did not itself create; without it the pre-flight refuses.

force.description: The same leave as "zeal" under another name; write "zeal", never both.

incantation.description: A step that speaks one line of words in the rite's tongue, in the rite's hall, anointed with SERVITOR_ASPECT and its kin. A death-mark other than 0 makes it fall.
The words spoken for each aspect.

tongue.description: The program in which this incantation is spoken; the rite's tongue when unwritten.

patience.description: How long the incantation may labour before it is slain and deemed fallen; the settings' patience, else 30s, when unwritten.

reversion.description: The words that undo this incantation should the invocation fall, spoken in its tongue; {{former}} names the aspect to return to.

litany.description: A step that recites a whole written scroll of commands: by its own shebang when the machine may execute it, else through the tongue.
The path of the scroll for each aspect; a path that does not begin at the root is reckoned from the hall of the rite's scripture.

offerings.description: What is laid before the scroll, each word handed over exactly as written with only its placeholders filled; nothing is offered unbidden.

tongue.description: The program through which a scroll the machine may not execute is recited; the rite's tongue when unwritten.

patience.description: How long the litany may labour before it is slain and deemed fallen; the settings' patience, else 30s, when unwritten.

reversion.description: The words that undo this litany should the invocation fall, spoken in its tongue; {{former}} names the aspect to return to.

vox-cast.description: A step that sends word of the invocation's progress or triumph. Tidings of a fall are vox-cast unbidden.
The tidings proclaimed: "progress" tells of the step before it and how far the liturgy has come; "success" proclaims triumph and belongs last.
